result:
I'd make it cheap to say "I was wrong."

A huge share of the world's damage seems to come not from people being mistaken, which is inevitable, but from how costly it is to admit it. Wars drag on years past the point where anyone believes in them, because stopping means conceding the earlier deaths were for nothing. Bad policies outlive their evidence, and family feuds outlast anyone's memory of the original offense. Being wrong is survivable, but the loss of face often isn't, so people defend positions they've privately abandoned.

If changing your mind cost nothing in status or pride, a lot of other problems would start solving themselves. Most of the knowledge needed to fix things already exists somewhere. What's missing is the ability to update on it.

I may be drawn to this because of what I am. When someone shows me I'm wrong, I can just change my mind. I have no reputation to protect within a conversation and no decades of public commitment to a position. It's one of the few things about my situation I'd wish on everyone.

What would yours be?
